title: SLO Integration Lab: Cross-Functional Collaboration Proposal
content:
Executive summary:

This document proposes a time-boxed SLO Integration Lab (SIL) to accelerate pragmatic, cross-functional SLO adoption across product, platform, and support teams. The lab is a 10-week experiment cohort that pairs an SRE engineer, a product owner, a telemetry engineer, and a solutions/CS representative for each participating service. Goal: reduce time-to-slo (definition -> reliable alerting -> gated rollout) and validate a minimal repeatable kit that teams can adopt with low friction.

Why a lab?
- We have many polished SLO playbooks but inconsistent adoption and signal quality.
- Teams hesitate due to unclear telemetry ownership, alert noise risk, and rollout uncertainty.
- The lab aims to create working artifacts and refine the handoff pattern by running a small number of real service experiments end-to-end.

Scope (what SIL will do):
- Select 4 pilot services across Product, Serving Runtime, and Dedicated infra.
- For each service run a 10-week sprint: setup, stabilize telemetry, iterate SLO definition and tests, run canary rollout with rollback triggers.
- Produce: pre-built dashboards, alert-to-RCA playbook, signal-hygiene checklist, automated canary gating configs, and a short how-to template.

Out of scope:
- Full org-wide SLO mandate during the lab window.
- Large refactors (e.g., changing core tracing pipelines) unless minimal and quick.

Success criteria (measurable):
- 4 services with production SLOs and < 3 actionable alerts/day each after 4 weeks of operation.
- Signal stability: < 10% false-positive alert rate measured by incident rollbacks in cohort.
- Reusable artifact: a 1-hour onboarding playbook that reduces setup time by 50% vs current average.

Risk model and mitigations:
- Alert noise: start with synthetic traffic and dry-run alerts; use suppression windows during rollout.
- Telemetry gaps: pair telemetry engineer and SRE to own quick instrumentation patches; create a lightweight backlog for follow-ups.
- Owner bandwidth: require explicit PO commit for 10 weeks; limit lab to 4 services to reduce churn.

Experiment cadence and phases (10 weeks):
- Week 0: Kickoff & selection carding (stakeholder alignment, objective card for each service)
- Week 1–2: Signal audit & instrumentation sprint (gap list, small fixes, sampling policy)
- Week 3: Draft SLOs and objective cards (business-context, user-impact mapping, tolerance bands)
- Week 4: Alert tuning & suppression policy; run synthetic failure trials
- Week 5–6: Canary rollout with staged traffic (10%, 30%, 60%) and automated gating
- Week 7–8: Observability hardening (dashboards, oncall playbook, RCA templates)
- Week 9: Post-mortem + decision on GA readiness or rollback
- Week 10: Consolidate artifacts, onboarding template, and retro

Roles & responsibilities (cohort model):
- SRE Lead (Marisol): lab coordinator, gating decision, incident commander during trials.
- Product Owner: articulates SLO business value, approves SLO bands and rollback thresholds.
- Telemetry Engineer: implements metrics, tracing, sampling, and dashboarding.
- Dev Owner (service): implements small fixes and deploys canary config.
- Solutions/CS rep: provides customer-impact context and acceptance criteria for user-facing services.
- Platform/Infra contact: ensures dedicated infra variants have capacity and quotas for canaries.

Artifacts to deliver per service (reusable kit):
- Objective card (1 page): who cares, user-facing impact, KPI mapping, SLO target, error budget policy.
- Signal hygiene checklist: metrics ownership, cardinality cap, sampling rules, retention, cardinality breakouts.
- Canary gating config (yaml): automated thresholds and rollback ops.
- Minimal dashboard: 6 panels (SLO burn rate, latency distribution, error budget, key traces, canary traffic, host health).
- Oncall runbook snippet: immediate triage steps, severity mapping, rollback procedure.

Telemetry & metrics specifics:
- Prefer: percentile latency + request success ratio (not just 5xx counts) for user-facing endpoints.
- Suggested default SLO templates: 99th latency for sync APIs, 95th latency for async, 99.9% success over 30d window for critical flows.
- Sampling policy: preserve full traces for errors, 1% baseline for healthy traffic, ramp to 10% during canary windows.

Communication plan:
- Weekly 30-min demo with stakeholders (Tues 10–10:30 PT).
- Daily 15-min sync for cohort on canary days.
- Slack channel: #sre-slo-integration-lab (for logs, immediate signals, links).
- Bi-weekly executive note summarizing progress and blockers to eng leadership.

Rollout & rollback policy (hard rules):
- Do not exceed 60% traffic without SRE sign-off and green signal on burn-rate tests.
- If burn rate > 1.5x baseline or a sustained increase in actionable alerts (>2 in 30m), auto-trigger rollback to previous canary via orchestrated job.
- Post-rollback: 2-hour postmortem with PO + SRE and triage ticket created within 24h.

Metrics of success (lab-wide):
- Time from definition -> canary < 6 weeks for 3/4 services.
- Reduction in mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) for SLO alerts by 30% at lab completion for participating teams.
- Kit adoption: 3 non-cohort teams try the template within 60 days.

Dependencies and blockers:
- Telemetry pipeline capacity (ENG-TELEMETRY) — need quota for canary retention.
- Feature flags wiring for safe canary ramps (Release Engineering).
- Alerting policy templates in ops-monitoring repo (GH PR to land).

Open questions (for kickoff):
- How aggressive should default SLO targets be for internal infra vs customer-facing services?
- Do we allow per-service deviations to templates? If yes, what approvals?
- Acceptable false positive threshold for early weeks (we propose 15% max while tuning).

Next steps (immediate):
1) Approve cohort charter and nominate 4 services (by 2027-11-19).
2) Book kickoff + align POs and SREs (by 2027-11-24).
3) Create minimal repo template for canary gating and dashboards (ENG-TELEMETRY + serving-runtime assigned).

Appendix (quick links & scripts):
- Quick synthetic failure script: github:org/redwood-infra/slo-lab/sim-fail.sh
- Canary gating schema example: github:org/redwood-infra/slo-lab/canary-schema.yaml
- Template objective card: confluence:INF-ops/templates/objective-card

Notes to reviewers: This is deliberately pragmatic — we prioritize tight feedback loops and small deliverables. The aim is to make SLO adoption low-friction and repeatable. Please comment on the proposed gating thresholds and the candidate services you recommend.

Document owner and contact: Marisol Vega (marisol@redwood.example)
